title: GTA6 Ultimate Edition Proves Popular Despite Pricing Concerns, Take-Two Reveals
description: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick reveals that many players pre-ordering GTA6 are opting for the more expensive Ultimate edition over the standard version, defying pricing hesitation.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA6 Pre-Orders: Ultimate Edition Surprises with Strong Demand

As anticipation builds for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, pricing has consistently been one of the most talked-about topics within the gaming community. While many potential buyers have expressed hesitation at the idea of paying triple-digit figures for a video game, the reality of the pre-order market appears to tell a different story.

### The Allure of the Ultimate Edition

According to Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar's parent company Take-Two, a significant portion of consumers who have already pre-ordered Grand Theft Auto 6 are bypassing the $80 (£70) Standard edition in favor of the much more expensive Ultimate edition.

This trend highlights a fascinating dynamic in the modern gaming landscape. Despite initial pushback and general debate across forums and social media regarding the rising cost of AAA titles—with some balking at the prospect of spending around $100 (£90) for a game—the most dedicated fans are clearly showing a willingness to vote with their wallets for the premium tiers.

### What This Means for the Industry

Zelnick's recent insights suggest that for a blockbuster IP of this magnitude, the core audience remains largely unfazed by steep price tags when it comes to securing the definitive version of the experience. It underscores the unmatched market power of Rockstar Games and indicates that premium pricing strategies for flagship titles may continue to find a receptive audience among hyper-engaged players.

## Editor's Take

Strauss Zelnick's revelation proves that when it comes to GTA6, hardcore fans are willing to stretch their budgets. While a $100 price point sparks fierce debate, the strong uptake of the Ultimate edition shows that premier content still commands massive consumer loyalty.
